summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. She studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn (Magister ~1983, Dr. phil. ~1990), Marburg (Habilitation ~2001), and the Manjushree Centre. She served at Vienna (~2002–2003) and Marburg (Privatdozentin 2009).

Adelheid Mette (1934–2023) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Hamburg (Promotion 1958, Habilitation ~1972) under Ludwig Alsdorf. She served as professor at Münster (1971, 1988–2000) and held professorial posts at Munich (1978, 1980, 2000).

Aden Kumler is a historian and archaeologist educated at Chicago (BA), Toronto (MA), the Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies (Licentiate), and Harvard (PhD ~2007). She served at the University of Chicago (2007–2020) and became professor at Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche (1931–2007) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche, and later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère (1853–1917) worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He founded The Proletarian and La Typographie française, served as Résident de France at Kratie in Cambodia, and was co-founder and vice-president of Société Ethnologique de Paris.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye (1906–1975) was an Indologist who studied at Mumbai and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He was Lecturer at Rajaram College (1930–1962), Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University (1962–1971), and founding professor at Mysore (1971).

Adolf Attenhofer (1879–1950) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Geneva, Paris, Berlin, and Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He taught at Bündner Kantonsschule (~1906–1946) and founded and directed the Bündner Volkshochschule in 1924.

Adolf Erhart (1926–2003) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Masaryk University's Faculty of Arts under Václav Machek from ~1945 to 1949, later serving as professor at Masaryk University (1988–1993).

Adolf Erman (1854–1937) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist. Educated at Leipzig under Georg Ebers and at Berlin, he held long-standing posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1880–1923) and the Egyptian Museum of Berlin (~1883–1923).
Adolf Faust was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Strasbourg by 1877 and worked as a school-teacher (Professor) at the Gymnasium Mulhouse.

Adolf Friedrich (1914–1956) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Frankfurt under Leo Frobenius and Hermann Lommel, later holding Privatdozent posts at Vienna (1942), Mainz (1946), and Frankfurt (~1947–1954).
Adolf Friedrich Hermann Paul Gärtchen was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Breslau (1900–1905), where he studied under Otto Hoffmann and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (1807–1887) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Bonn, Berlin (PhD under Franz Bopp), and Paris. He served as professor (1833–1847) and Rektor (1862–1863) at the University of Breslau.

Adolf Friedrich von Schack (1815–1894) was a scholar in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed law studies between 1833 and 1838 at the universities of Bonn, Heidelberg, and Berlin.

Adolf Holtzmann (1810–1870) specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, Munich, and Paris under scholars including Eugène Burnouf and Othmar Frank. He held posts at Bismarck-Gymnasium Karlsruhe (1837) and Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Holtzmann Jr. (1838–1914) was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg under Adolf Holtzmann, Erlangen under Friedrich von Spiegel, and under Rudolf von Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Freiburg (1885–1914).

Adolf Janáček (1901–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. at Charles University (~1920–1924) and also studied at its Faculty of Arts, First Faculty of Medicine, and Teacher Examination Board.

Adolf Kaegi (1849–1923) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich (PhD), Leipzig, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He taught at Kantonsschule Rämibühl and was a professor at the University of Zurich from 1878 to 1914.

Adolf Kiessling (1837–1893) studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1854–1858). He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1858–1859), the University of Basel (~1869–1877), and the University of Greifswald (~1877–1889).

Adolf Kirchhoff (1826–1908) was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist educated at Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and served as professor at Berlin (1865–1908) and member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
